title: Oktoberfest and Scottish Festival grant funding restored
subtitle: Also: 84 Frederick Street cost increase, paramedic master plan, Lancaster Street expropriation, housing funding and delegations on vehicles and night trimming.
overview: Regional Council spent much of the evening on tourism grants. After a procedural tangle, it voted to use the Regional share of the hotel tax (MAT) reserve to restore KW Oktoberfest funding to $65,000 and Cambridge Scottish Festival funding to $10,000, voting on each separately.

Council also approved an extra $200,000 for the 84 Frederick Street renovation contract, with a related capital budget increase. It endorsed the 2026 paramedic response time targets, a Paramedic Services Master Plan for 2026 to 2035, and housing investment plans. Committee recommendations on water financial plans, the RetrofitWR home energy pilot and the Lancaster Street West expropriation in Kitchener were approved. A further conditional commitment for an affordable housing proposal passed {{vote:m9}}.

Delegations raised enclosed low-speed electric vehicles being sold as mobility devices, and overnight roadside trimming. Staff will report back on both. Council also heard updates on respiratory vaccines and on the Region's Truth and Reconciliation work. A closed session on litigation and labour matters was held, and the minutes record no public outcome.

decisions.detail: Council will use an additional $22,820 from the MAT reserve to restore KW Oktoberfest funding to $65,000 {{vote:m13}}.
Council will use an additional $1,080 from the MAT reserve to restore Cambridge Scottish Festival funding to $10,000 {{vote:m14}}.
Council increased the MMA Construction contract by $200,000 to $5,552,515.33 plus taxes and added $240,000 to the 2025 capital budget from the Homelessness Prevention Capital Reserve.
Council approved the Year 7 housing investment plan, the 2026 ambulance response time targets and the Paramedic Services Master Plan for 2026 to 2035, subject to annual budgets.

Council approved the Water Financial Plans, assumption of Oxford Road 5 in Wilmot, the RetrofitWR pilot agreements, expropriation for Lancaster Street West improvements, and adding Homer Watson Boulevard lands to the Regional road system.
Council authorized a further conditional letter of commitment, for up to one year, toward a long-term lease with the Central Ontario Co-Operative Housing Federation or an affiliate.
Council approved an updated Records Retention By-law, received the 2025 Mid-Year Update and amended the 2025 Capital Budget.
Council approved the 2026 to 2029 Library Service Delivery Plan in principle, subject to budget, plus a new Bequest Policy and revised Donations Policy.

debate: Several councillors objected that staff added the Scottish Festival to a report that Council had directed to cover only Oktoberfest, and that the festival had not asked for funds. One councillor said they could not justify giving money to a group they had not heard from.

Supporters of funding both said festivals add to quality of life and tourism, and are volunteer-run at low cost. One said Cambridge groups receive little from this fund. Staff said the goal was consistency with historical allocations and the grant formula, and that the program will be reviewed in the second year of the next mandate.

One councillor questioned supporting Oktoberfest when the food bank could not be fully funded, and asked about Oktoberfest's reserves. Staff said its financials are public and it is financially sound.

A procedural dispute arose over whether an amendment dropping the Scottish Festival was effectively a contrary motion. It ended with an amendment that split the funding so each part could be voted on separately.

On night trimming, staff said contractors work overnight for traffic safety and to avoid throwing debris at traffic. Electric trimmers are being tested, and a weed-management pilot is planned in Cambridge. A delegate said the work woke neighbours and the safety argument was weak.
